ant_intro_html:
Same pipeline, unchanged code, on the paper's main benchmark: Visual AntMaze (OGBench medium maze, 64×64 pixels from a back camera, 8-D torque actions, success = within 1.0 maze unit of the goal, 350-step budget). Model: pretrained 2-level H-JEPA, seed 42, with the official ant_l2 planner (level-2 GD 90 iterations × 200 samples, level-1 GD 90 × 25, replanning every 10 steps). Test = the official 50 tasks; RASR train (40) and val (20) tasks come from the official grid generator under a different seed, and the code asserts that no start–goal configuration is shared. Env resets are seeded (100000 + task) as on FourRoom.

Unlike FourRoom, failed AntMaze episodes mostly show the ant stalling against a wall or circling near its start, i.e. the low-level controller does not execute the subgoal. That is the case reachability-aware planning is meant for.
ant_p1_html:
Labels as on FourRoom: from every 2nd (train) or 3rd (val/test) planning call of baseline episodes, the simulator state is restored and the frozen level-1 MPC executes the baseline's subgoal for 60 steps with three budgets (B0 2×4, B1 10×20, B2 90×25 = default). A subgoal counts as reached within H ∈ {10, 20, 40, 60} steps if the real level-2 latent comes within eps = 12.06 of it (median latent distance of train frame pairs closer than 0.5 maze units, half the success radius, the same ratio as FourRoom's 8 / 16 px). Restored states are exact (replaying the logged actions from a snapshot reproduces xy with zero error). Renders match to ≤ 1/255 at every call except the first one after reset, where a few isolated pixels differ (task 1: 6 of 4 096 pixels, mean 0.09/255).

The learned predictors do not beat the distance reference here. The logistic on ‖g − z‖² and the controller condition is best on val (AUROC 0.869 vs 0.829 for the MLP) and on test, and it is the one used by the planner (val-selected). The MLP runs are kept as an ablation.
droid_intro_html: DROID in H-JEPA is open-loop planning on recorded real-robot clips: the planner proposes an action sequence from the first frame and a goal frame, and the official metric compares it to the expert's actions (Fréchet fidelity = 1 − F(plan, expert) / F(zero motion, expert)). Nothing can be executed, so this is not a closed-loop test and there is no success rate and no local repair. What can be checked is the P1 + P2 part: whether a reachability score over the level-2 candidate subgoals changes the selected plan, and whether that improves fidelity.
droid_p1_html: Without a controller, the label comes from the expert video: the j-th level-2 subgoal of a candidate plan (level-2 stride 3 frames, 0.6 s) is labelled reachable if it comes within eps of a real expert frame encoding by the time the plan wants to be there (eps = 14.63, median latent distance of expert frames one level-2 step apart, train clips). Candidate pools: 16 level-2 GD samples per clip on 160 train / 40 val clips from DROID training shards (deterministic 80/20 split by episode) and the 16 evaluation clips as test. As on AntMaze, the distance logistic beats the MLP on val and test, so it is the planner's predictor.
droid_p2_html: The planner's level-2 candidate is chosen by cost − λ · c_min · mean_j log(R_j + δ); λ = 0 is the unmodified planner and reproduces the official eval.py output exactly (Fréchet 0.3809, ATE 0.1584 on planner seed 1). Predictor and λ were selected on 24 val clips only.
droid_after_html:
No effect on DROID. Reranking changes the chosen plan on 30 of 48 test runs, but fidelity is unchanged within noise. The val gain of the selected setting (+0.3 points over λ = 0) was already inside the spread of the other settings.

Why no effect

  • The predictor is not the problem. Within one clip it ranks the candidates by their true label with Spearman 0.74 (MLP 0.66), and candidates do differ (on-path fraction from 0.0–0.2 up to 0.4–1.0 per clip).
  • The offline label mostly means “the subgoal stays near the start”. 90% of positive labels match one of the first three expert frames (first 0.6 s), and the positive rate falls from 64% at the first subgoal to 6% at the last. A plan that barely moves is “on the expert path” under a min-over-frames label, which is why the distance to the current state alone reaches AUROC 0.98.
  • So reranking buys conservatism, which the metric does not reward. On the 30 changed runs, the selected candidate has higher mean R (0.18 → 0.39) and an 8% higher progress cost. Fréchet fidelity is measured relative to zero motion, so a plan that moves less does not score better. The fidelity change is uncorrelated with the gain in R (Spearman 0.07) and with the cost given up (0.06).
  • Little room to choose. The released droid_l2 planner keeps only 4 level-2 candidates per clip (the labels were collected with 16).

A time-aligned label removes the “don't move” shortcut. It was run after this result as a post-hoc follow-up (below).
droid_aligned_html: Post-hoc, motivated by the analysis above, so it is reported separately and not as the pre-planned test. Subgoal j now counts as reachable only if it matches an expert frame within 3j ± 3 frames, i.e. near the time the plan wants to be there. Same clips, eps, candidate pools and selection protocol (predictor ∈ {MLP, distance logistic} × λ ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}, plus λ = 0, chosen on the 24 val clips). The positive rate drops from 24% to 13% (train), and the distance to the current state alone is now a much weaker predictor (AUROC 0.89 instead of 0.98), so the label carries more than “stay close”. The distance logistic (on ‖g − z0‖² and log H) is again best on val.
droid_aligned_after_html: Still no significant effect. With the aligned label the selected setting changes 19 of 48 test selections and moves fidelity by +0.5 points (38.85% vs 38.31%), well inside the seed-to-seed spread of the baseline (±0.9), with as many clips better as worse. Reachability-aware selection therefore does not help open-loop DROID planning with either label. The likely remaining reasons are the small candidate pool (4 per clip) and that open-loop fidelity only rewards matching the expert, not executability.
ant_p23_method_html: Same methods and val-selected hyper-parameters as FourRoom (B3 λ = 0.25, Ours β = 20, same monitor and repair), with AntMaze ε, kernel width and controller condition (H = 10, B2). The planner's predictor is the val-selected distance logistic. The MLP versions of B3 and Ours are run as an ablation. One planner seed (42) on the 50 official test tasks.
ant_table_note: McNemar p is the exact two-sided test against B1 on the same 50 tasks. Wilson 95% intervals in brackets. Even B3, which only reorders candidates, flips 7 of 50 tasks, so single-seed differences below about ±6 tasks are within noise.
ant_results_html:
On AntMaze, repair helps, and the reachability term hurts, at every seed. Over three planner seeds (150 episodes per method), the repair without R (Ours−R) reaches 54.0 ± 1.2% vs 38.0 ± 2.0% for the baseline (+33 / −9 episodes, pooled McNemar p < 0.001) and is ahead at each seed (54/56/52% vs 36/42/36%). This is the only significant improvement in the project. Full replanning on the same trigger (B4) reaches 48.0% (+23 / −8, p = 0.01); Ours−R vs B4 is +20 / −11 (p = 0.15). Adding the reachability term to the repair and the selection (Ours) drops success to 26.7%, below the baseline (+12 / −29, p = 0.01; against Ours−R +7 / −48, p < 0.001). Reranking alone (B3) does nothing (35.3%, p = 0.60), and replanning twice as often (B2, seed 42 only, 2× compute) gives 44% (p = 0.42).

Why R hurts here

  • The selected predictor is essentially a distance prior. The distance logistic scores a subgoal by how close it is to the current latent. With it, reranking raises the median R of the chosen subgoal from 0.43 to 0.89 and changes 61% of selections at almost no cost on the planner's own objective (median ×1.01). In other words, it picks the nearest of the near-equivalent candidates.
  • In the repair, this undoes the exploration term. The repair is triggered because the ant is stuck. The novelty penalty pushes the new subgoal away from visited states, and the R term pulls it back towards the current state. Without R, the repair moves the subgoal away and the ant gets unstuck. B4, which replans from scratch, shows the same direction.
  • The MLP predictor is less extreme (median R 0.57 → 0.73, 43% changed), and Ours-MLP lands at 38%, between the two.

Ours−R was a pre-planned ablation, not chosen on test, and the seed-43/44 runs were added after the seed-42 result as a replication; they confirm it. The same ordering (Ours−R best, Ours not better than B1) was seen on FourRoom, where it was not significant. B2 was run for seed 42 only (it doubles the planning cost). The diagnosis below uses the seed-42 runs.
ant_seeds_note: Same model (seed 42), same 50 official tasks and environment seeds; only the planner seed changes. Pooled McNemar: exact two-sided test against B1 over the 150 task × seed pairs. Seed 42 is the run in the table above; seed 42 of B1 was re-run through the seed-job path and reproduces it exactly.
